report:
**Conclusion:** Yes, treatment with cortisone-like drugs (systemic corticosteroids such as dexamethasone) significantly reduces mortality and improves survival among critically ill COVID-19 patients who require respiratory support.

**Key Evidence:**

1. **The RECOVERY Trial:** This major randomized controlled trial demonstrated that dexamethasone (6 mg daily for up to 10 days) reduced 28-day mortality by approximately one-third in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation and by one-fifth in patients receiving supplemental oxygen without ventilation. However, dexamethasone showed no benefit—and potential harm—for mild cases not requiring oxygen (NEJM: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436).

2. **Mechanism:** Severe COVID-19 can trigger a massive inflammatory response ("cytokine storm") causing lung injury and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Corticosteroids suppress this hyperinflammatory tissue destruction.

3. **Global Guidelines:** Pooled meta-analyses across international trials led the World Health Organization (WHO) to issue strong recommendations advocating systemic corticosteroids as standard-of-care for severe and critically ill COVID-19 patients (WHO: https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-updates-clinical-care-guidance-with-corticosteroid-recommendations ; https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/coronaviruse/module-3-corticosteroid-therapy-and-covid19.pdf).

In summary, corticosteroids significantly improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients who require oxygen or mechanical ventilation.
